_comment: The workflow registry. A capability is an entry here, not code: build the
graph in ComfyUI, export it with Save (API Format) into this directory,
add an entry, restart. No backend changes.
Node IDs are brittle -- they change if a graph is rebuilt in the editor --
so every template is versioned in its filename and every binding below is
checked against the template at boot. A mismatch fails loudly at startup,
never silently at generation time. Run `alchemyui validate` to check by
hand, or `alchemyui validate --live` to also ask a running ComfyUI whether
the node classes and checkpoints actually exist.

txt2img-sdxl._est_note: Seeds the ETA until real runs are observed, then an EWMA takes over. seconds_per_step is measured on a GTX 1660 Ti Mobile (6GB, --fp8_e4m3fn-unet): SDXL 1024x1024 x25 steps = ~131s wall. load_s is deliberately conservative -- an observed 3.8s was a page-cache-warm read, not a cold one.

inpaint-sdxl._grow_mask_note: ComfyUI's own default is 6, which leaves a visible ring around the mask on a 1000px-ish image: RealVisXL is not an inpainting checkpoint, so it refills the blanked region with a slightly different colour balance. 32 was measured to reduce that markedly. Higher values blend better but regenerate more of what you kept, which is why the slider goes to 64.

enhance-sdxl._chain_note: Two settings were tuned against measured runs on a GTX 1660 Ti rather than taken from the node defaults. force_inpaint is False in the template: with it True, Impact Pack falls back to sampling the entire crop whenever the detected face is already larger than guide_size, which on a portrait means re-rendering the whole image for no resolution gain (~5 minutes here). False makes it skip that case, which is the point of a detail pass. refine_steps is 14, not 25: the hi-res pass runs at denoise 0.35, so 25 steps traverses the same short stretch of the schedule far more finely than the result justifies.

likeness-sdxl._faceid_note: face_weight and face_weight_v2 are IPAdapterFaceID's two strengths; the spec asks for both as sliders because they trade off differently. When a personal LoRA is active the app lowers the default face weight to ~0.45: the LoRA and FaceID both encode identity and fight each other at full strength. provider is CPU in the template because onnxruntime-gpu is not installed and the GPU belongs to the sampler.
